newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says most activities better in 1996.
newsitem.headline: ING says most activities better in 1996.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Thursday almost all of its banking, insurance and investment activities improved results in 1996 due to a worlwide increase in total income.

The group, which bought collapsed British merchant bank Barings in 1995, earlier announced a 25.4 percent leap in net profit to 3.32 billion guilders for 1996, at the upper end of analysts' expectations.
It said profit from insurance activities rose 18.6 percent to 2.50 billion guilders, with banking profits increasing 21.7 percent to 2.13 billion.
Exchange rate changes contributed 41 million to the pre-tax result.
The tax burden however eased to 26.4 percent in 1996, compared with 29.9 percent a year earlier.

ING said total assets grew by 22.1 percent to 483.9 billion guilders at December 31 while shareholders equity surged 43.5 percent to 34.1 billion, due mainly to the increased value of the insurance operations' equity investments.
Within the insurance operations, life premium income grew considerably, especially in Australia, North America and Japan, while the Dutch life operations showed handsome growth.
The group said that in life insurance, where pre-tax profits grew 10 percent, results were gratifying again in the Netherlands and they showed strong growth in Hungary and Japan.
But life results from North America fell due to a non-recurring lower result in Canada and a strengthening of insurance funds in the United States.
Non-life insurance profits rose 28.9 percent, mainly due to higher results in the Netherlands and Australia, but the U.S. result was marred by a severe winter and storms.
The fire business slumped to a loss due partly to the U.S. weather conditions.
The health result was also a loss, mainly because of its North American operations.
Higher dividend and investment income were the main factors behind the 27.5 percent increase in general insurance profits.
ING said that within the banking business, net interest income grew 15.9 percent, helped by a slight widening of the interest margin and strong growth in assets.

Commission income leapt 33.7 percent, reflecting the consolidation of Barings and Poland's Bank Slaski, the excellent stock market climate and higher corporate finance commissions and asset management fees.

Results from financial transactions jumped 25.9 percent as favourable market conditions boosted securities trading results by 71.7 percent and because the 1995 result was low in the wake of the Mexican currency crisis.
But currency trading profits fell 42.4 percent from the incidentally high level of 1995.

ING said value adjustments to the receivables of the banking operations rose 3.7 percent, against a 21.2 percent increase in banking lending. "The lower increase of the addition to the provision reflects the improving quality of the lending portfolio," it said.
